model.name: Nav2 1.1.20 likelihood_field
model.distance_function: map_update_cspace, called on private offline memory

contents.algorithm: Original CAD collision triangles; physical face normals; conservative actual XY triangle projection; existing free cells retained; other cells unknown.

normal_criterion.justification: Structural near-vertical surfaces; excludes the 42 degree traversable corrugation slope and horizontal support surfaces; fixed before scoring any scan.

height_filter.reason: Recorded LaserScan has no original hit z; no unmeasured narrow slice is assumed. Actual per-cell contributing face z ranges are preserved.

rasterization.amcl_model_note: Score with unchanged upstream MAP_GXWX; no half-cell shift or evaluation-pose registration.

limits: Horizontal top surfaces and oblique ramps may still appear in the unchanged terrain-derived scan and are not represented by this candidate
Visibility/occlusion not encoded in 2D surface union
Per-cell z bounds are conservative contributing-triangle extrema
Comparison must preserve all exact recorded scan pairs and original AMCL likelihood semantics

scope_boundaries: Only exact-stamp published AMCL pose/scan pairs are scored; other received scans retain counts and explicit rejection reasons.
A published posterior pose is a representative estimate, not the entire particle set; scores do not reconstruct filter stochastic history.
Two recorded poses are compared. No pose optimization, map translation, control correction, or truth input to localization is performed.
An offline candidate scores the same recorded runtime AMCL/evaluation poses; it does not claim a new native localization result.
Truth is independently recorded evaluation data; no timestamp extrapolation or last-value holding is allowed.
Primary scoring is the same planar model at both poses; full-transform XY residuals and scan-plane tilt expose projection differences.
Structure tiles locate nearby occupied PGM cells; they do not identify CAD materials or prove a physical object label.
A score preference alone does not establish whether filtering noise, terrain projection, or map semantics caused localization error.
Coverage is restricted to recorded finite beams and the declared session, with no full-field accuracy claim.
